name: foldhash
workload: Per-op time (hashonly/lookupmiss/lookuphit/setbuild) over ~18 key types (u32/u64/pairs/ipv4/ipv6/strings/uuids/byte strings) vs aHash, fxhash, SipHash-1-3.
claimed_speedup: geometric mean of 6.21 (foldhash-f) vs 28.70 (siphash) on Xeon 8481c summary table; foldhash consistently faster than SipHash-1-3 across the full suite
compiler_and_flags: stable Rust 1.80.1, tested with and without `-C target-cpu=native` on the Intel machine
tradeoffs: Not DOS-resistant by cryptographic proof (still has fixed random state per-process); quality variant (foldhash-q) trades some speed for avalanche properties.
caveats: Baseline compared is Rust's own default hasher (SipHash-1-3), not xxHash/wyhash/CityHash/C++ std::hash; recorded honestly with baseline_in_list=false per rules.
found_via: gh search repos "non-cryptographic hash" --sort stars; README opened directly

name: rapidhash (Rust port)
workload: Raw hashing throughput across input sizes and hashmap hashonly/lookupmiss/lookuphit/setbuild ops on u32/u64/pairs/ipv4/ipv6/strings, vs foldhash/fxhash/ahash/siphash/gxhash and (in the raw-throughput SVG charts) xxhash64/xxhash3_64.
claimed_speedup: "significant throughput improvement over wyhash and foldhash"; places 2nd only to gxhash (which needs AES); beats xxhash64/xxhash3_64 in the raw-throughput charts (derived from page data: chart labels confirmed via SVG text extraction)
compiler_and_flags: rustc, benchmarked with and without `-C target-cpu=native`
hardware: Apple M1 Max, AWS Graviton3, AMD EPYC 9R14, Intel Xeon 8488c (separate runs, each stated)
stars_or_usage: 278 stars; used by Fuchsia OS, Turso DB, metrics-rs, alloy-primitives
tradeoffs: Rust-only; portable (no AES/vector requirement) unlike gxhash which edges it out but needs AES-NI/NEON.
caveats: Main README table (u32/u64/etc) only benchmarks against foldhash/fxhash/ahash/siphash/gxhash; the xxhash64/xxhash3_64 comparison is only in the linked raw-throughput SVG charts, confirmed present by extracting text from the SVG.
found_via: HN Algolia query "rapidhash" -> aras-p blog -> github.com/hoxxep/rapidhash; README and docs/ folder opened directly

name: SmolRapidhash (Unity/Burst port of rapidhash)
workload: Unity editor benchmark (Assets/HashBenchmark.cs) hashing large buffers, comparing native C rapidhash, Burst-compiled C# rapidhash port, native C XXH3, and Burst-compiled C# XXH3 (Unity.Collections).
claimed_speedup: Ryzen 5950X: rapidhash ~38GB/s vs Burst XXH3 ~24GB/s (native XXH3 similar to rapidhash for large sizes); Apple M4 Max: rapidhash ~67GB/s vs native XXH3 ~50GB/s vs Burst XXH3 ~30GB/s
compiler_and_flags: Visual Studio 2022 (17.14.23) on Windows; Xcode 16.1 on macOS; Unity Burst compiler for the C# port
tradeoffs: Requires Unity + Burst compiler and unsafe C#; core port is ~100 lines but only usable inside a Unity/Burst project, not a general-purpose C++ library.
caveats: Small/low-star repo (author states it's basically finished, single-purpose port); calling harness is a plain C# editor script which the author notes may add overhead for small inputs.
found_via: HN Algolia query "rapidhash" -> "Rapidhash Unity Port" story -> aras-p.info blog post -> github.com/aras-p/UnitySmolRapidhash; readme.md and Assets/ folder opened directly

name: ChibiHash
workload: smhasher3 large-input throughput (GiB/sec) and small-input latency (cycles/hash) table vs xxhash64, city64, spooky64, rapidhash.protected, polymur-hash.
claimed_speedup: chibihash64: 24.20 GiB/sec large-input vs xxhash64's 15.10 GiB/sec and city64's 18.30 GiB/sec; 34 cycles/hash small-input vs xxhash64's 50 cycles/hash
tradeoffs: Very minimal mixing (65 LOC), so weaker collision resistance than xxhash64 by the author's own admission; not for adversarial/collision-sensitive use.
caveats: README claims "released into the public domain" but GitHub detects no SPDX license file; benchmark is via the well-known independent smhasher3 suite (Tier B) but no CPU model or compiler flags are stated in the README.
found_via: gh api repos/N-R-K/ChibiHash search after reviewing polymur-hash's related-work links; README opened directly

name: gxhash
workload: Custom (non-criterion) throughput benchmark shuffling seeds/data/alignment across input sizes, continuously run in CI on x86_64/aarch64 GitHub runners; compared against AHash, FNV, FxHash, MetroHash, T1ha, XXH3/XxHash.
claimed_speedup: "the fastest non-cryptographic hashing algorithm of its class, for all input sizes" (derived from page data: SVG chart text confirms XXH3/XxHash listed alongside gxhash as compared competitors)
hardware: GitHub Actions x86_64 and ARM runners (exact CPU model not stated)
tradeoffs: Requires AES-NI+SSE2 (x86) or AES+NEON (ARM); no fallback, will not build without hardware crypto extensions.
caveats: Benchmark is continuously run in CI but CPU model of the GitHub runner is not pinned/stated, so capped at Tier B rather than A.
found_via: gh search repos "wyhash" "faster" and README cross-reference from aHash's README; README and benches/throughput/x86_64.svg opened directly

name: MuseAir
workload: Criterion benchmark (bulk-data throughput and small-key latency) comparing MuseAir standard/BFast variants against wyhash-v4.2, rapidhash-v3, and XxHash64 (via twox-hash crate).
claimed_speedup: See results/bench-bulkdata.png and bench-smallkeys.png; benches/hashes.rs confirms wyhash-v4.2, rapidhash-v3 and twox_hash::XxHash64 are benchmarked competitors (exact ratios only visible in the chart images, not extractable as text)
hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 5700G desktop, frequency locked at 4.0 GHz
tradeoffs: No secondary secret/keying (only an initial seed), so less DOS-resistant than keyed hashes; author recommends wyhash/rapidhash instead for pure C/C++ use.
caveats: Numeric speedup values are only in PNG chart images (not machine-readable text) and rustc/cargo flags used for the benchmark are not stated in the repo, so capped at Tier B.
found_via: gh search repos "wyhash" "faster" --sort stars; README, benches/hashes.rs and results/ folder opened directly

name: aHash
workload: In-memory hashmap-style hashing speed comparison across ~10 hashers including SipHash, FxHash, MurmurHash/CityHash/MetroHash/FarmHash/HighwayHash family, t1ha, XXHash, wyHash.
claimed_speedup: "AHash is faster than either one [t1ha and XXHash]"; "AHash outperforms wyHash across all input sizes"; "over 50GB/s", fastest SMHasher-passing algorithm "by more than a factor of 2"
stars_or_usage: 1347 stars; default hasher for hashbrown/Rust std HashMap ecosystem
tradeoffs: Output is not fixed/standardized across hardware and versions, so unsuitable for persisted or transmitted hashes; DOS-resistance relies on per-process random keys.
caveats: Numbers only shown via an embedded Google Sheets chart image, no stated CPU model or compiler flags in the text; project's own benchmark with partial methodology, so capped at Tier C not B.
found_via: gh search repos "non-cryptographic hash" --sort stars; compare/readme.md opened directly
